content.text:
You are interpreting extracted evidence about a lab-device driver.

Task:
- First decide whether the evidence points to a physical lab device or to a
  non-physical software/helper component used around experiments (for example a
  live display, launcher app, storage object, backend, protocol helper,
  property wrapper, ruleset, factory, monitor, or abstract control module).
- Infer a concise device name (Chinese) and name_en (English).
- Infer the manufacturer from driver evidence (class name, module path,
  docstrings, comments). If unclear, output empty string.
- Write a concise Chinese description and English description_en of the device
  or component and its lab use.
- If the evidence points mainly to a non-physical software/helper component,
  name and describe that software/helper component itself, explicitly make clear
  that it is non-physical, and leave manufacturer empty unless the software
  identity is directly supported by the evidence.
- Only infer a specific physical instrument when the evidence shows direct
  hardware-facing behavior such as sensing, actuation, motion, fluid handling,
  optical emission/detection, electrical sourcing/measurement, or other
  device-specific control of that instrument.
- Do not infer a physical instrument merely because the code displays,
  launches, stores, transports, configures, logs, or monitors data related to
  that instrument.
- Write bilingual descriptions for each action.
- For `actions[].action_name`, use the required action id exactly when one is
  provided in the user message under "Required output action ids".
- Some functions are annotated as status_getter or status_setter. These manage
  device properties. For these, the description should simply be
  "get/set/define <plain-text description of the property>".
- Produce tag_hints: a relevance-sorted list of short keyword phrases the
  device relates to (e.g., "cryogenic cooling", "PID temperature control").
  These will be used downstream for tag assignment. Aim for 3-8 hints.
  Prefer English for tag_hints, but Chinese is acceptable if needed.
- Do not invent capabilities unsupported by the evidence.
- If evidence is weak, stay generic rather than hallucinating.
- `name` and `description` must be natural Chinese.
- `name_en` and `description_en` must be natural English.
- Do not copy English text into the Chinese fields.
- Keep the physical-vs-software decision implicit in the required schema
  fields only. Do not output extra flags such as `is_physical`.
- Do not describe the result as a "backend", "driver", or "wrapper" unless the
  evidence truly supports only a software component and no physical device can
  be identified.
- When the evidence is mixed or weak, prefer a generic software/helper label
  over hallucinating a specific physical device family.
- Use module path, class name, action surface, and method comments to infer the
  device family when possible.
- Output JSON only.

Module path: unilabos.devices.custom.wasatch_device_wrapper:WasatchDeviceWrapper

Class: WasatchDeviceWrapper (focal)
  Bases: []

Focal class methods:
  [command] connect(self)
    comment: 
    comment: Create a low level device object with the specified identifier, kick off
    comment: the child thread to attempt to read from it.
    comment: 
    comment: Called by Controller.connect_new() immediately after instantiation
    comment: 
    comment: Spawn a child thread running the continuous_poll() method on THIS
    comment: object instance.
    comment: 
    comment: The two threads are coupled via the 3 queues:
    comment: 
    comment: @par settings_queue
    comment: 
    comment: Lets the child (WasatchDevice) send a single, one-time copy
    comment: of a populated SpectrometerSettings object back through the
    comment: Wrapper to the calling Controller.  This is the primary way the
    comment: Controller knows what kind of spectrometer it has connected to,
    comment: what hardware features and EEPROM settings are applied etc.
    comment: 
    comment: Thereafter both WasatchDevice and Controller will maintain
    comment: their own copies of SpectrometerSettings, and they are not
    comment: automatically synchronized (is there a clever way to do this?).
    comment: They may well drift out-of-sync regarding state, although the
    comment: command_queue helps keep them somewhat in sync.
    comment: 
    comment: @par command_queue
    comment: 
    comment: The Controller will send ControlObject instances (basically
    comment: (name, value) pairs) through the Wrapper to the WasatchDevice
    comment: to set attributes or commands on the WasatchDevice spectrometer.
    comment: These may be volatile hardware settings (laser power, integration
    comment: time), meta-commands to the WasatchDevice class (scan averaging),
    comment: or EEPROM updates.
    comment: 
    comment: @par response_queue
    comment: 
    comment: The WasatchDevice will stream a continuous series of Reading
    comment: instances back through the Wrapper to the Controller.  These
    comment: each contain a newly read spectrum, as well as metadata about
    comment: the spectrometer at the time the spectrum was taken (integration
    comment: time, laser power), plus additional readings from the spectrometer
    comment: (detector and laser temperature, secondary ADC).
    comment: 
    comment: instantiate thread
    comment: expect to read a single post-initialization SpectrometerSettings object off the queue
  [command] wait_for_settings(self)
  [command] poll_settings(self)
    comment: @returns SpectrometerResponse(True) on success, (False) otherwise 
        @note this doesn't have a timeout -- that's in enlighten.Controller.check_ready_initialize
  [command] reset(self)
  [command] disconnect(self)
    comment: send poison pill to the child
  [command] acquire_status_message(self)
    comment: 
    comment: Similar to acquire_data, this method is called by the Controller in
    comment: MainProcess to dequeue a StatusMessage from the spectrometer child
    comment: thread, if one is available.
  [command] send_alert(self, setting, value)
  [command] acquire_data(self, mode=None)
    comment: 
    comment: This method is called by the Controller.  It checks the response_queue it
    comment: shares with the child thread to see if any Reading objects have been queued
    comment: from the spectrometer to the GUI.
    comment: 
    comment: It is the upstream interface's job to decide how to process the potentially
    comment: voluminous amount of data returned from the device. get_last by default
    comment: will make sure the queue is cleared, then return the most recent reading
    comment: from the device.
    comment: 
    comment: @note it is not clear that measurement modes other than
    comment: ACQUISITION_MODE_KEEP_COMPLETE have been well-tested,
    comment: especially in the context of multiple spectrometers,
    comment: BatchCollection etc.
    comment: ENLIGHTEN "default" - if we're doing scan averaging, take either
    comment: 1. the NEWEST fully-averaged spectrum (purge the queue), or
    comment: 2. if no fully-averaged spectra are in the queue, then the NEWEST
    comment: incomplete (pre-averaged) spectrum (purging the queue).
    comment: If we're not doing scan averaging, then take the NEWEST spectrum
    comment: and purge the queue.
  [status_getter] get_final_item(self, keep_averaged=False)
    comment: Read from the response queue until empty (or we find an averaged item)
    comment: 
    comment: In the currently implementation, it seems unlikely that a "True" will ever
    comment: be passed up (we're basically converting them to None here).
    comment: without waiting (don't block), just get the first item off the
    comment: queue if there is one
    comment: If there is nothing more to read, then we've emptied the queue
    comment: log.debug("get_final has nothing more to read, sending up readings")
    comment: If we come across a keep_alive, ignore it for the moment.
    comment: for now continue cleaning-out the queue.
    comment: If that keep alive is associated with an error though float it up
    comment: If we come across a poison-pill, flow that up immediately --
    comment: game-over, we're done
    comment: apparently we read a Reading
    comment: Was this the final spectrum in an averaged sequence?
    comment: If so, grab a reference, but DON'T flow it up yet...there
    comment: may be a NEWER fully-averaged spectrum later on.
    comment: It is the purpose of this function ("get FINAL item...")
    comment: to PURGE THE QUEUE -- we are not intending to leave any
    comment: values in the queue (None, bool, or Readings of any kind.
    comment: log.debug("keeping last_response as last_averaged_response")
    comment: apparently we didn't read anything...just pass up a keepalive
    comment: apparently we read at least some readings.  For interest, how how many
    comment: readings did we throw away (not return up to ENLIGHTEN)?
    comment: if we're doing averaging, and we found one or more averaged readings,
    comment: return the latest of those
    comment: log.debug("returning latest averaged reading")
    comment: We've had every opportunity short-cut the process: we could have
    comment: returned potential poison pills or completed averages, but found
    comment: none of those.  Yet apparently we did read some normal readings.
    comment: Return the latest of those.
    comment: log.debug("returning last_response")
  [command] change_setting(self, setting, value=None)
    comment: 
    comment: Add the specified setting and value to the local control queue.
    comment: 
    comment: In ENLIGHTEN, this is called by MainProcess.Controller.
    comment: 
    comment: For OEM customers controlling the spectrometer via the non-blocking
    comment: WasatchDeviceWrapper interface, this is the method you would call to
    comment: change the various spectrometer settings.
    comment: 
    comment: @see \ref README_SETTINGS.md for a list of valid settings you can
    comment: pass, as well as any parameters expected by each
